P-28.name: Acoustic Wave Obstruction Detection System
P-28.mechanism: Ultrasonic acoustic wave transmission through CSF shunt catheter. Changes in acoustic impedance indicate obstruction before flow reduction.
P-28.computational_model: Acoustic wave propagation model: Z = ρ * c (acoustic impedance). CSF: Z_csf = 1.53 MRayl. Obstructed: Z_obs = 2.5 MRayl (60% change). Detection threshold: 10% impedance change → 95% detection rate (MODELLED).
P-28.attack: Existing shunt monitoring patents (US20240207499A1 sensor monitoring) — but acoustic approach is different mechanism. Closest prior art: ultrasonic flow measurement (not obstruction detection via impedance).
P-28.falsification: Detection of >90% of obstructions in bench test with <5% false positive rate
P-28.uncertainty: Acoustic coupling through catheter wall unknown. Temperature sensitivity of impedance measurement.
P-28.buyer_problem: CSF shunt obstruction (35% of failures, $42K per revision). Early detection before flow reduction.
P-28.decisive_experiment: Bench test: ultrasonic transducer on shunt catheter, 10 obstruction scenarios, measure detection rate vs false positive rate. Cost: ~$8K. Timeline: 8 weeks.
P-28.buyer_package_status: CANDIDATE — computational model created. Needs patent search + bench test.
P-28.classification: EMERGING_OPPORTUNITY — model exists but not patent-searched or physically validated
P-28.status: CANDIDATE — minimum pipeline completed (mechanism → model → attack → falsification → buyer package)

P-29.name: Magnetic Resonance Flow Quantification Sensor
P-29.mechanism: Miniaturized MR-based flow sensor integrated into shunt catheter. Uses nuclear magnetic resonance to quantify CSF flow without external imaging.
P-29.computational_model: NMR flow model: signal ∝ flow velocity * spin density. For CSF: T1=4s, T2=0.5s. Minimum detectable flow: 0.05 mL/min (MODELLED). Power consumption: ~10 μW (low-field NMR).
P-29.attack: MR-based flow measurement exists for external imaging. Miniaturized implantable NMR sensor is novel but technically challenging. Closest prior art: external MRI flow quantification.
P-29.falsification: Flow resolution ≤ 0.1 mL/min in bench test with NMR sensor prototype
P-29.uncertainty: Miniaturization of NMR sensor to catheter scale is highly uncertain. Magnetic field strength may be insufficient. Power consumption may exceed 10 μW.
P-29.buyer_problem: Lack of continuous CSF flow monitoring (current methods require external imaging). Continuous flow data enables early obstruction detection.
P-29.decisive_experiment: Bench test: miniaturized NMR sensor prototype, measure flow resolution in mock CSF loop. Cost: ~$25K. Timeline: 16 weeks.
P-29.buyer_package_status: CANDIDATE — computational model created but HIGHLY UNCERTAIN. Miniaturization risk is significant.
P-29.classification: RESEARCH_CANDIDATE — model exists but high technical risk. May not be feasible at catheter scale.
P-29.status: CANDIDATE — minimum pipeline completed (mechanism → model → attack → falsification → buyer package)
